newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha eases, backwardation steeper.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha eases, backwardation steeper.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices dipped in Tokyo trade on Friday, but the loss was small given a sharp fall in overnight crude oil prices, traders said.
"Naphtha could have lost further if it were not for the support from healthy regional fundamentals," one trader said.
Backwardation in inter-month spreads steepened amid tight prompt supplies, traders said.
The one-month spread from first-half April was discussed at plus $10.00/11.00 after changing hands once at $10.00, and again at $10.60, on Thursday.
Also on Thursday, first-half May/first-half June was sold from a European trader to a Japanese trading house at $6.50.
Bids for second-half April open-spec naphtha were heard at $234.00 per tonne with no offers having emerged. The offer levels were assessed at $236.00.
It was quoted at $236.00/237.00 in late-Thursday trading.
First-half May was indicated about $5.00 lower than the second-half April levels.
In middle distillates, spot jet cargoes for March delivery were notionally assessed at $1.80 to $2.00 over the mean of Singapore quotes in quiet trading. -- Tokyo Energy Desk
